title: Isometric illustration / Usage

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content area, default interactive state

slide_intent: Preserve a believable spatial frame while objects move so viewers can understand depth and cause and effect.
strategic_value: Consistent perspective and physical weight can make IBM’s architectural illustration language useful for complex concepts.
demonstration: Application mockups precede a layered-cube sequence and paired motion examples for translation, rotation, camera, shading and weight.
practical_value: Animate along the isometric grid and evaluate whether each movement preserves the scene’s perspective.

content_islands.name: Applications
content_islands.spec: Begin with reports, diagrams, product screens and printed communications.

content_islands.name: Animation model
content_islands.spec: Introduce the layered blue cube and tips on volume, shadows and physicality.

content_islands.name: Perspective comparisons
content_islands.spec: Group translation, rotation and camera pairs around the cube motif.

content_islands.name: Shading and physicality
content_islands.spec: Finish with 2D-gradient and weight comparisons, retaining their explanatory captions.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text explains that violating the grid breaks the illusion of space and depth.
reference_purposes.Expression: Blue volumetric forms use a fixed isometric frame.
reference_purposes.Application: Pairs demonstrate one-axis translation and rotation, fixed-camera behavior and shading choices.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The page calls for one-axis motion and a locked isometric camera, with only rare controlled camera repositioning; it discourages baked 3D gradients and exaggerated motion.

ingredient.name: Isometric motion frame
ingredient.application: Move along the 30° construction grid, usually on one axis at a time; keep the camera fixed and make shadows respond to the objects.
ingredient.scope: IBM isometric illustrations, typically produced as 2D artwork. The source preserves rare controlled-camera exceptions and selective rotation.
